captions.01_setup: Eight half-wavelength-spaced sensors observe zero-mean complex snapshots. The hidden spatial line and its posterior are inferred from passive covariance information; the desired steering vector enters only the beamforming decision.
captions.02_information: One-snapshot Fisher information is isotropic in the 14 real native-complex tangent coordinates. Small score-covariance residuals are Monte Carlo fluctuations, not population anisotropy. Physical arrival-angle information is a separate pullback along the ULA steering curve, in inverse radians squared.
captions.03_tracking: The physical moving-ULA record is preassigned trial zero at s=0.2. The scan uses modal covariance, not the actual beamforming weights. Noise and truth-dependent drift budgets are evaluated at predeclared fixed times; drift is unavailable to the estimator. Only valid certificates are compared with actual modal error; the valid long stationary cohort has n=4.
captions.04_decisions: Each scatter point is an independent training stream at N=8. Posterior expected-power optimality does not imply a win at every true covariance. The complete horizon/noise map retains losses; open circles mark paired pointwise 95% intervals containing zero. Purple boxes mark exact one-snapshot isotropization ties. The final panel is the actual weight beampattern, not covariance scanning power.
captions.05_uncertainty: The preassigned stationary-ULA record at N=8 shows scalar central 50/95% power quantiles and, separately, the image of one common 95% state HPD region. The scalar inclusion experiment uses three fixed angular queries, averaged within each trajectory before uncertainty across independent trajectories. At an exact interferer query the truth s+q is a support endpoint and finite continuous-posterior equal-tail intervals exclude it. These fixed-state checks are distinct from prior-predictive Bayesian calibration.
captions.05_state_coverage: Fixed stationary states, known powers, n=8 and independent observation streams. Markers show the fraction of true states contained in the computed 95% HPD region or posterior ball, with pointwise 95% Wilson binomial intervals. The horizontal scale is the full 0 to 1 coverage range. Eight cells are displayed without a simultaneous or all-cells calibration claim. State-region numerical flags are separate from scalar-tail flags; unresolved state calculations are marked rather than excluded.
captions.06_prediction_and_risk: The cloud is only the two-coordinate projection Re/Im(e2^H P v), not a full-state credible region. The directional risk curve is derived from the same saved posterior mean M using v^H(M-M^2)v; these queries are not known training inputs. Binned risk checks use independent random-query trajectories, averaging queries within each trajectory, with pointwise Student intervals across independent trajectories.
captions.07_parameter_inference: The joint posterior of s=b and q=a-b and data-amount intervals use preassigned stationary trial zero. The last panel averages independent streams at N=32 and scores the next observation and next true covariance before assimilation. Prospective log density and output power are different losses. A filled joint point requires parameter and joint covariance-mean diagnostics; the full-state tail diagnostic is reported separately. Horizontal bars show only 1.96 times the recorded score Monte Carlo standard error of the mean, not variability across data sets or a convergence certificate for the full mixture density.
captions.08_process_and_cost: The native eight-sensor complex predictive moment law is checked against independent transition draws, including real and imaginary entries. Exact first-moment matching does not imply exact predictive density: the separate two-channel CP1 reference reports density total variation against inverse-moment residual. Timings cover native numerical operations, not end-to-end comparisons against tracking algorithms. The full report includes its nested sampling and moment work and should not be added to those rows.
